newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel, unleaded basis steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel, unleaded basis steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel differentials were steady on Tuesday but seen firming on a bullish inventory report released late in the day, traders said.
The American Petroleum Institute said PADD II unleaded gasoline stocks were drawn down 481,000 barrels last week and remained 2.1 million barrels below the same week last year.

Distillate stocks on hand in primary storage at Midwest refineries were drawn down 1 million barrels on the week, and refinery utilization stood at 94.6 percent of capacity, down 0.1 percentage points, the trade group said.
"This might push basis a bit higher," one trader said of the API weekly inventory survey.

Earlier in the day, the Williams pipeline system reported a 41 day supply of low sulphur diesel fuel and 22 day supply of unleaded gasoline on hand, down from seasonal-high levels posted last month, traders said.
Low sulphur diesel was bid 0.75 cent a gallon over NYMEX March heating oil in Group Three and 1.75 cents over the print in Chicago for prompt barrels, traders said.
High sulphur diesel was bid 2.50 cents under the print in Group Three and even with the print in Chicago.
Unleaded gasoline was talked 0.25 cent under to even with NYMEX March unleaded in Group Three and 2.50/2.25 cents under the print in Chicago.
Jet/kero firmed to 3.25/3.50 cents over the print in Group Three and 3.75/4.0 cents over in Chicago, continuing a steady climb of late.
